result.summary: This PR is a large refactor of net_processing.cpp (plus txrequest, txdownloadman, addrman, net.h, and related files) to replace ad-hoc integer/duration time representations with typed NodeClock::time_point and NodeSeconds values. It fixes places still using the deprecated GetTime() call, converts fields like m_stalling_since, m_last_block_time, m_next_inv_send_time, and m_downloading_since to time_point types, and introduces sentinel usage (epoch, min, max) for unset states. Ten commits were iteratively reshaped based on review feedback, including splitting out behavior-labeled vs pure-refactor commits.
result.problem: Bitcoin Core's p2p and mempool code mixed integer, duration, and time_point representations of time, which the author describes as 'confusing' and error-prone, making the code harder to reason about and review. This affects maintainers and reviewers of net_processing, txrequest, and eviction logic.

open_concerns: ryanofsky maintains that expanding use of the nonstandard NodeClock::epoch constant is bad practice and encourages footguns, though he ACKed the PR anyway (agree-to-disagree).
stickies-v prefers std::optional over min()/max() sentinels for fields like m_stalling_since and m_next_inv_send_time; author declined citing added complexity, stickies-v accepted as non-blocking.
jeanpablojp left three nits (passing `now` consistently, using PowTargetSpacing(), and eviction test precision) explicitly marked non-blocking.
resolved_concerns: Commit message clarity about behavior vs pure-refactor commits was addressed by splitting commits and rewording messages.
Concern about test hardcoding of microseconds was addressed by author explaining fuzz-input format constraints; reviewer accepted (thumbs up).
Confusing sentinel semantics for m_stalling_since/m_headers_sync_timeout were improved by switching some fields from epoch-zero to min()/max().

result.card: This PR is a refactor of Bitcoin Core's net_processing.cpp and related p2p files (txrequest, txdownloadman, addrman, net.h, util/time.h) to replace ad-hoc integer or duration time representations with typed NodeClock::time_point/NodeSeconds values, fixing lingering uses of the deprecated GetTime(). It solves a maintainability pain point for anyone touching peer eviction, tx-download, or address-manager time logic, per the author's stated goal to make time handling in net_processing 'properly use time_point types.' It has been extensively reviewed (six distinct reviewers, ACKs from stickies-v, ryanofsky, jeanpablojp, sedited, seduless, concept ACK from w0xlt) with a persistent but non-blocking disagreement between ryanofsky and the author over using NodeClock::epoch as a sentinel value, resolved by agreeing to disagree. The PR is currently marked Needs rebase and the author has been silent since 2026-07-21, so mechanical staleness rather than code quality is blocking further review. No PR dependency is stated, though the author suggests a possible follow-up PR to fully remove epoch usage, and a reviewer flagged a possible interaction with the scoped-clock proposal in #35557.
